description: Regroup BrowserSettingsSheet.kt into the six sections of design image 12_PhoneBrowserSettings.png, in this exact order: START UP (Home page, Default gradient background), APPEARANCE (Display scale slider), IN-APP CONTROL (Always show floating button, Floating button action, Floating button position), CONTENT BLOCKING & SITE (Block ads and trackers, User agent), PLAYBACK (YouTube add-ons nav row, DRM Widevine L3 enforcer), PRIVACY AND SITE DATA (Clear browsing data, Delete cookies and site data, Reset saved site permissions). This is a reordering of the render() method — every existing control and store call is kept; the 'Appearance' segmented row that currently exists is NOT in the design (the design's APPEARANCE section is only the display-scale slider), so verify against the current spec before removing it (see steps). Add a new 'YouTube add-ons' nav row that opens YouTubeSettingsActivity. Independent of FEAT-001 and FEAT-003.
steps: 1. Read context.json first. Read BrowserSettingsSheet.kt fully — note render() builds the column in this current order: Appearance (segmented light/dark), Display scale, Start up (Home page + launch behavior), In-app control (Floating action, Always show floating, Floating position), Start page (gradient toggle), User agent, Playback (DRM), Content blocking (ad block), Privacy and site data (reset permissions, delete cookies, clear data).

2. Reorder render() to match design 12 exactly:
   sectionLabel('Start up'):
     - homePageRow()  (Home page → onEditHomePage, shows 'Start page' subtitle)
     - the gradient-background toggleRow currently under 'Start page' section — MOVE it here. Title 'Default gradient background', subtitle 'Draw the start page over the app's gradient', BrowserStartupStore.gradientBackground/setGradientBackground + onStartPageBackgroundChanged().
   sectionLabel('Appearance'):
     - displayScaleRow()  (the slider; shows e.g. '110%')
   sectionLabel('In-app control'):
     - toggleRow('Always show floating button', ...) BrowserControlsStore.alwaysShowFloatingButton
     - floatingActionRow()  ('Floating button action' → cycles)
     - floatingPositionRow()  ('Floating button position' Left/Right segmented)
   sectionLabel('Content blocking & site'):
     - toggleRow('Block ads and trackers', ...) BrowserAdBlock
     - userAgentRow()  ('User agent' → onEditUserAgent, Mobile/Desktop/Custom)
   sectionLabel('Playback'):
     - NEW navRow('YouTube add-ons', <subtitle>) that opens YouTubeSettingsActivity. Since the sheet has an activity reference, call activity.startActivity(dev.autobridge.youtube.YouTubeSettingsActivity.intent(activity)). Subtitle e.g. 'SponsorBlock and playback quality'. Use a new string.
     - toggleRow('DRM Widevine L3 enforcer', ...) BrowserDrmStore
   sectionLabel('Privacy and site data'):
     - navRow('Clear browsing data', ...) onClearBrowsingData
     - navRow('Delete cookies and site data', ...) onDeleteSiteData
     - navRow('Reset saved site permissions', ...) onResetPermissions
   Note design order within Privacy: Clear browsing data FIRST, then Delete cookies, then Reset permissions.

3. The current 'Appearance' section is a light/dark segmented control (BrowserAppearanceStore). Design image 12's APPEARANCE section shows ONLY the Display scale slider — there is no light/dark segmented control visible. Per the constraint 'Do NOT delete UI that isn't explicitly marked REMOVE': the design does not mark it REMOVE, it is simply not shown in this crop. SAFE CHOICE: keep the appearance (light/dark) segmented control but move it so it does not conflict with the design's APPEARANCE=display-scale labeling. Place the light/dark segmented row under a small 'Theme' handling: EITHER keep it as a second row inside the APPEARANCE section (slider first, then the light/dark segmented), OR leave it where visually sensible. Decision: keep appearanceRow() inside the APPEARANCE section, rendered AFTER displayScaleRow(). This preserves the control (no deletion) while matching the section name. If the reviewer/design owner later marks it REMOVE, it can be dropped in a follow-up — do not delete it now.

4. Add string resources (EN values/strings.xml + TH values-th/strings.xml). The sheet currently uses hardcoded English strings for section labels and row titles (e.g. 'Start up', 'Block ads and trackers'). This FEAT does NOT need to externalize all of them (out of scope — keep existing hardcoded literals as-is to avoid churn), EXCEPT the one NEW user-facing row 'YouTube add-ons' and its subtitle, which should use new string keys for EN+TH consistency with the rest of the app:
   - browser_settings_youtube_addons  EN='YouTube add-ons'  TH='ส่วนเสริม YouTube'
   - browser_settings_youtube_addons_caption  EN='SponsorBlock and playback quality'  TH='SponsorBlock และคุณภาพการเล่น'
   Rename the section header literal 'Content blocking' to 'Content blocking & site' (the design's wording). Rename literal 'Start page' section (gradient toggle) — that section is being merged into 'Start up', so the standalone 'Start page' sectionLabel is removed and its toggle moves under 'Start up'.

5. Confirm no store call changed — every BrowserStartupStore / BrowserControlsStore / BrowserDisplayScaleStore / BrowserAppearanceStore / BrowserAdBlock / BrowserDrmStore / BrowserUserAgentStore read/write stays identical, only row ORDER and section LABELS change. This guarantees every preference key is preserved.
6. Confirm the build passes: ./gradlew testPersonalDebugUnitTest assemblePersonalDebug
acceptance_criteria: BrowserSettingsSheet render() produces sections in this order: Start up, Appearance, In-app control, Content blocking & site, Playback, Privacy and site data.

Start up contains Home page + Default gradient background. In-app control contains all three floating-button controls. Content blocking & site contains Block ads + User agent. Playback contains YouTube add-ons (new) + DRM. Privacy and site data contains Clear browsing data, Delete cookies, Reset permissions (in that order).
The light/dark appearance segmented control is NOT deleted (kept inside Appearance section after the slider).
Every store read/write is unchanged — no preference key altered.
New EN+TH strings added; no existing string removed or renamed.
findings: Reordered BrowserSettingsSheet.render() into the six design-12 sections in exact order: Start up (Home page + Default gradient background toggle moved out of the old 'Start page' section), Appearance (displayScaleRow slider then the light/dark appearanceRow kept — not deleted, placed after the slider per step 3), In-app control (Always show floating button toggle, Floating button action, Floating button position), Content blocking & site (Block ads + User agent), Playback (NEW YouTube add-ons nav row + DRM Widevine L3), Privacy and site data (Clear browsing data, Delete cookies, Reset permissions in that order). The standalone 'Start page' and 'Display scale'/'User agent'/'Content blocking' section labels were folded into the new sections; label 'Content blocking' -> 'Content blocking & site'. New nav row opens YouTubeSettingsActivity via activity.startActivity(YouTubeSettingsActivity.intent(activity)). Added strings browser_settings_youtube_addons / _caption in both values/ (EN) and values-th/ (TH); no existing string renamed or removed. Every store read/write (BrowserStartupStore, BrowserControlsStore, BrowserDisplayScaleStore, BrowserAppearanceStore, BrowserAdBlock, BrowserDrmStore, BrowserUserAgentStore) is byte-for-byte identical — only row order and section labels changed, so all preference keys are preserved. Build gate: ./gradlew testPersonalDebugUnitTest assemblePersonalDebug -> BUILD SUCCESSFUL (warnings pre-existing, unrelated). Note: visual section-by-section compare against docs/design/12_PhoneBrowserSettings.png on a device remains the human reviewer's final gate.
